items.title: GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints
items.tldr: Introduced grouped-query attention — sharing each key/value head across a group of query heads — cutting KV-cache memory several-fold with near-zero quality loss; now the default attention configuration in almost every open LLM
items.key_contribution: Interpolated between multi-head and multi-query attention by grouping query heads over shared KV heads, plus a cheap uptraining recipe to convert existing MHA checkpoints — hitting multi-query speed at multi-head quality, which made it the universal deployment default (Llama 2/3, Mistral, Qwen, Gemma)
items.display_name: GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints
items.summary: Introduced grouped-query attention — sharing each key/value head across a group of query heads — cutting KV-cache memory several-fold with near-zero quality loss; now the default attention configuration in almost every open LLM

items.title: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning
items.tldr: Bridged a frozen vision encoder and a frozen LLM with trainable cross-attention (Perceiver Resampler + gated cross-attention), enabling few-shot vision-language tasks from interleaved image-text prompts — the template most modern VLMs follow.
items.key_contribution: Showed how to graft visual perception onto a pretrained LLM without retraining either: a Perceiver Resampler compresses variable image features into a fixed set of tokens, and gated cross-attention layers inserted into the frozen LLM let it attend to images, giving strong few-shot multimodal learning from interleaved prompts.
items.display_name: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning
items.summary: Bridged a frozen vision encoder and a frozen LLM with trainable cross-attention (Perceiver Resampler + gated cross-attention), enabling few-shot vision-language tasks from interleaved image-text prompts — the template most modern VLMs follow.

items.title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
items.tldr: Trains an LM to emit reflection tokens deciding when to retrieve and whether retrieved passages support its output — making retrieval adaptive and self-critiqued instead of always-on, and improving factuality over standard RAG
items.key_contribution: Introduced trainable reflection tokens ([Retrieve], ISREL, ISSUP, ISUSE) that let one model control retrieval timing, grade passage relevance, and verify its own grounding during generation — with inference-time control over the factuality/fluency trade-off via token-probability thresholds
items.display_name: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
items.summary: Trains an LM to emit reflection tokens deciding when to retrieve and whether retrieved passages support its output — making retrieval adaptive and self-critiqued instead of always-on, and improving factuality over standard RAG

items.title: K9-Bench: Evaluating Multimodal LLMs on Canine-Centric Videos
items.tldr: A 5,000-pair question set over 907 home dog videos, built to test long-horizon reasoning about canine actions and interactions.
items.key_contribution: Roughly 5,000 curated pairs over 907 real videos, which is large enough for a per-category breakdown rather than a single noisy score.
items.display_name: K9-Bench: Evaluating Multimodal LLMs on Canine-Centric Videos
items.summary: A 5,000-pair question set over 907 home dog videos, built to test long-horizon reasoning about canine actions and interactions.

items.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
items.tldr: Trained a harmless assistant using AI self-critique and AI-judged preferences instead of human harm labels -- consider RLAIF when human labeling of harmful content is a bottleneck, though no reference code exists to reproduce it directly
items.key_contribution: Showed a model can be trained to be harmless using only a written list of principles (a 'constitution') plus its own self-critique and self-generated preference judgments, replacing human-labeled harm data with AI-generated feedback (RLAIF)
items.display_name: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
items.summary: Trained a harmless assistant using AI self-critique and AI-judged preferences instead of human harm labels -- consider RLAIF when human labeling of harmful content is a bottleneck, though no reference code exists to reproduce it directly

items.title: AGC-Bench: Measuring Artificial General Creativity
items.tldr: An 78-dataset creativity benchmark paired with AGC-Judge, an open-weight judge calibrated to remove leniency bias.
items.key_contribution: Judge bias is corrected psychometrically rather than ignored, which is the difference between a usable creative ranking and a self-fulfilling one.
items.display_name: AGC-Bench: Measuring Artificial General Creativity
items.summary: An 78-dataset creativity benchmark paired with AGC-Judge, an open-weight judge calibrated to remove leniency bias.

items.title: Managing Procedural Memory in LLM Agents: Control, Adaptation, and Evaluation
items.tldr: Introduces AFTER, a 382-task benchmark for testing whether procedural skills learned by agents transfer across tasks, roles, and model backbones.
items.key_contribution: Separates local improvement from cross-task, cross-role, and cross-model transfer, showing that multi-model execution traces can produce more portable skills than single-model traces in the reported study.
items.display_name: Managing Procedural Memory in LLM Agents: Control, Adaptation, and Evaluation
items.summary: Introduces AFTER, a 382-task benchmark for testing whether procedural skills learned by agents transfer across tasks, roles, and model backbones.

items.title: Graph of Thoughts: Solving Elaborate Problems with Large Language Models
items.tldr: Generalizes chain- and tree-of-thought by modeling reasoning as an arbitrary graph, where thoughts can be aggregated, refined, and looped -- enabling operations like merging partial solutions that a tree cannot express
items.key_contribution: A reasoning framework (GoT) that represents LLM thoughts as vertices in a graph with edges as dependencies, supporting aggregation (combining thoughts), refinement (looping on a thought), and generation, which subsumes chain-of-thought and tree-of-thought as special cases and improves quality/cost on tasks with mergeable sub-solutions
items.display_name: Graph of Thoughts: Solving Elaborate Problems with Large Language Models
items.summary: Generalizes chain- and tree-of-thought by modeling reasoning as an arbitrary graph, where thoughts can be aggregated, refined, and looped -- enabling operations like merging partial solutions that a tree cannot express

items.title: Improving Language Models by Retrieving from Trillions of Tokens
items.tldr: RETRO augments a Transformer with chunk-level retrieval from a trillions-of-tokens database via cross-attention, letting a small model match much larger ones -- retrieval as a way to move knowledge out of parameters and into an index
items.key_contribution: A retrieval-augmented architecture that fetches nearest-neighbor text chunks from a massive external database and integrates them through a dedicated chunked cross-attention (CCA) mechanism, showing a 7.5B model can rival models 25x larger by offloading factual knowledge to the retrieval store rather than parameters
items.display_name: Improving Language Models by Retrieving from Trillions of Tokens
items.summary: RETRO augments a Transformer with chunk-level retrieval from a trillions-of-tokens database via cross-attention, letting a small model match much larger ones -- retrieval as a way to move knowledge out of parameters and into an index

items.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
items.tldr: Showed scaling a decoder-only Transformer to 175B params produces strong few-shot in-context learning with zero gradient updates, meaning you can often solve a new task via prompting instead of fine-tuning
items.key_contribution: Demonstrated that in-context learning (performing a task from a few prompt examples with no weight updates) emerges and improves predictably as model scale increases, without a scale-specific architectural change
items.display_name: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
items.summary: Showed scaling a decoder-only Transformer to 175B params produces strong few-shot in-context learning with zero gradient updates, meaning you can often solve a new task via prompting instead of fine-tuning

items.title: Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration Framework with Multiple Decoding Heads
items.tldr: Speeds up decoding by adding a few extra prediction heads that guess several future tokens at once, verified in parallel with tree attention — no separate draft model, 2-3x faster, and self-contained enough to bolt onto an existing model.
items.key_contribution: Made speculative decoding practical without a separate draft model: train lightweight extra heads on the base model's own hidden states to propose multiple continuations, then verify candidate token trees in a single forward pass via tree attention — retaining the base model's output distribution while cutting decoding steps.
items.display_name: Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration Framework with Multiple Decoding Heads
items.summary: Speeds up decoding by adding a few extra prediction heads that guess several future tokens at once, verified in parallel with tree attention — no separate draft model, 2-3x faster, and self-contained enough to bolt onto an existing model.

items.title: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code (Codex / HumanEval)
items.tldr: Introduced Codex (the model behind GitHub Copilot) and HumanEval with the pass@k metric — establishing execution-based functional correctness, not text similarity, as the way to evaluate code generation
items.key_contribution: Two exports that outlived the model: HumanEval, 164 hand-written programming problems evaluated by running unit tests, and the unbiased pass@k estimator — replacing BLEU-style text matching with 'does the code actually work' as the field's code-eval standard
items.display_name: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code (Codex / HumanEval)
items.summary: Introduced Codex (the model behind GitHub Copilot) and HumanEval with the pass@k metric — establishing execution-based functional correctness, not text similarity, as the way to evaluate code generation

items.title: UniClawBench: A Universal Benchmark for Proactive Agents on Real-World Tasks
items.tldr: Evaluates proactive agents on 400 bilingual real-world tasks in live Docker environments using capability-specific checkpoints and hidden closed-loop supervision.
items.key_contribution: Separates skill usage, exploration, long-context reasoning, multimodal understanding, and cross-platform coordination instead of mixing them into one scenario label.
items.display_name: UniClawBench: A Universal Benchmark for Proactive Agents on Real-World Tasks
items.summary: Evaluates proactive agents on 400 bilingual real-world tasks in live Docker environments using capability-specific checkpoints and hidden closed-loop supervision.

items.title: AgenticSTS: A Bounded-Memory Testbed for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
items.tldr: Tests a bounded-memory contract in which a long-horizon agent receives typed retrieval in a fresh prompt instead of an ever-growing raw transcript.
items.key_contribution: Separates memory and skill interventions from transcript growth, then evaluates the contract on a reproducible Slay the Spire 2 testbed with recorded trajectories and prompt conditions.
items.display_name: AgenticSTS: A Bounded-Memory Testbed for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
items.summary: Tests a bounded-memory contract in which a long-horizon agent receives typed retrieval in a fresh prompt instead of an ever-growing raw transcript.

items.title: Chatbot Arena: An Open Platform for Evaluating LLMs by Human Preference
items.tldr: Formalized the crowdsourced pairwise-battle leaderboard: anonymous side-by-side model comparisons on live user prompts, ranked with Bradley-Terry statistics — the methodology behind LMArena, the de facto public preference ranking for frontier models
items.key_contribution: Built and validated the open evaluation platform where users vote between two anonymous model responses to their own prompts, with a rigorous statistical pipeline (Bradley-Terry estimation, confidence intervals, efficient sampling) — establishing live human preference as a first-class benchmark complementary to static test sets
items.display_name: Chatbot Arena: An Open Platform for Evaluating LLMs by Human Preference
items.summary: Formalized the crowdsourced pairwise-battle leaderboard: anonymous side-by-side model comparisons on live user prompts, ranked with Bradley-Terry statistics — the methodology behind LMArena, the de facto public preference ranking for frontier models

items.title: PaLM: Scaling Language Modeling with Pathways
items.tldr: 540B dense transformer trained across two TPU pods — the era's peak few-shot results, the canonical documentation of emergent abilities at scale, and the demonstration that chain-of-thought unlocks reasoning at sufficient size
items.key_contribution: The scaling era's high-water-mark systems and science paper: Pathways-orchestrated training at 6144 TPUs with full logging of discontinuous improvements (BIG-bench breakthrough curves), and the PaLM+CoT result on GSM8K that made 'reasoning emerges with scale' the field's operating assumption
items.display_name: PaLM: Scaling Language Modeling with Pathways
items.summary: 540B dense transformer trained across two TPU pods — the era's peak few-shot results, the canonical documentation of emergent abilities at scale, and the demonstration that chain-of-thought unlocks reasoning at sufficient size

items.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning from Human Preferences
items.tldr: The origin of RLHF: learn a reward model from human comparisons of trajectory pairs, then optimize a policy against it — solving tasks where the objective is easier to recognize than to specify, with under 1% of interactions needing human feedback
items.key_contribution: Established the two-model pattern behind all modern alignment training: fit a Bradley–Terry reward model to pairwise human preferences, train the policy against the learned reward asynchronously — demonstrating that scalable human oversight of RL is possible at ~0.1% feedback density
items.display_name: Deep Reinforcement Learning from Human Preferences
items.summary: The origin of RLHF: learn a reward model from human comparisons of trajectory pairs, then optimize a policy against it — solving tasks where the objective is easier to recognize than to specify, with under 1% of interactions needing human feedback

items.title: Training Verifiers to Solve Math Word Problems
items.tldr: The GSM8K paper: released the 8.5K grade-school math benchmark that anchored LLM reasoning evaluation for years, and introduced verifier-guided sampling — train a model to judge candidate solutions, sample many, pick the best — the seed of verification-based test-time compute
items.key_contribution: Two contributions that outlived each other's context: GSM8K, the standard multi-step arithmetic-reasoning benchmark, and the verification paradigm — a trained verifier reranking sampled solutions beat a 30x-larger fine-tuned model, the founding result for solution-level verification and test-time compute scaling
items.display_name: Training Verifiers to Solve Math Word Problems
items.summary: The GSM8K paper: released the 8.5K grade-school math benchmark that anchored LLM reasoning evaluation for years, and introduced verifier-guided sampling — train a model to judge candidate solutions, sample many, pick the best — the seed of verification-based test-time compute

items.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
items.tldr: Reframed attention as an IO problem: tiling and online softmax keep the computation in GPU SRAM, avoiding materializing the N×N matrix — exact attention, 2-4x faster and linear memory, now compiled into effectively all training and serving stacks
items.key_contribution: Showed attention is bottlenecked by HBM memory traffic, not FLOPs, and gave an IO-optimal tiled algorithm (online softmax + recomputation in backward) computing exact attention without ever materializing the attention matrix — making long context computationally practical and obsoleting most approximate-attention research
items.display_name: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
items.summary: Reframed attention as an IO problem: tiling and online softmax keep the computation in GPU SRAM, avoiding materializing the N×N matrix — exact attention, 2-4x faster and linear memory, now compiled into effectively all training and serving stacks

items.title: FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Parallelism and Work Partitioning
items.tldr: Rewrote FlashAttention to cut non-matmul FLOPs, parallelize across sequence length, and partition work better between GPU warps — roughly 2x faster than v1 and reaching 50-73% of A100 peak, the kernel now underpinning most training and long-context serving.
items.key_contribution: Re-engineered the FlashAttention algorithm around GPU execution realities: minimizing expensive non-matmul operations, adding parallelism over the sequence dimension (not just batch/heads), and improving warp-level work partitioning to reduce shared-memory traffic — closing most of the gap to peak GPU throughput for exact attention.
items.display_name: FlashAttention-2: Faster Attention with Better Parallelism and Work Partitioning
items.summary: Rewrote FlashAttention to cut non-matmul FLOPs, parallelize across sequence length, and partition work better between GPU warps — roughly 2x faster than v1 and reaching 50-73% of A100 peak, the kernel now underpinning most training and long-context serving.

items.title: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
items.tldr: DeepSeek-V3: a 671B-parameter MoE (37B active) trained for a reported ~$5.6M of GPU time that matched frontier closed models — proof that systems co-design (MLA, FP8 training, aux-loss-free MoE routing, MTP) collapses the frontier cost curve
items.key_contribution: Demonstrated frontier-class capability at an order-of-magnitude lower reported training cost via co-designed innovations: Multi-head Latent Attention (KV-cache compression), auxiliary-loss-free MoE load balancing, multi-token prediction, and validated large-scale FP8 mixed-precision training — with open weights and an unusually detailed systems writeup
items.display_name: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
items.summary: DeepSeek-V3: a 671B-parameter MoE (37B active) trained for a reported ~$5.6M of GPU time that matched frontier closed models — proof that systems co-design (MLA, FP8 training, aux-loss-free MoE routing, MTP) collapses the frontier cost curve

items.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
items.tldr: Showed RL with automated, verifiable rewards (not human labels) can train strong reasoning directly, then distills into smaller dense models -- consider RL-from-verifiable-rewards for reasoning-heavy domains, not just human-feedback alignment
items.key_contribution: Demonstrated that reasoning capability can be incentivized through large-scale reinforcement learning using automated, verifiable rewards (correct/incorrect answers, not human preference judgments), without a supervised fine-tuning cold-start, and that this capability distills effectively into smaller dense models
items.display_name: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Showed RL with automated, verifiable rewards (not human labels) can train strong reasoning directly, then distills into smaller dense models -- consider RL-from-verifiable-rewards for reasoning-heavy domains, not just human-feedback alignment

items.title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
items.tldr: Showed you can fine-tune a 4-bit-quantized frozen base model with LoRA adapters trained in full precision, meaning you should use QLoRA when you need to fine-tune a large model on a single consumer GPU that couldn't otherwise fit it
items.key_contribution: Combined 4-bit NormalFloat quantization of frozen base-model weights with LoRA adapters kept in higher precision, plus paged optimizers to avoid memory spikes, cutting fine-tuning memory requirements enough to fine-tune a 65B model on a single 48GB GPU
items.display_name: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
items.summary: Showed you can fine-tune a 4-bit-quantized frozen base model with LoRA adapters trained in full precision, meaning you should use QLoRA when you need to fine-tune a large model on a single consumer GPU that couldn't otherwise fit it

items.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
items.tldr: Showed bidirectional masked-language-model pretraining beats left-to-right pretraining, meaning you should reach for an encoder-only model (not a decoder-only LLM) for classification/embedding tasks
items.key_contribution: Established masked-language-model pretraining (predicting randomly masked tokens using both left and right context) as a way to pretrain deep bidirectional representations, where prior approaches could only pretrain unidirectionally or shallowly-bidirectionally
items.display_name: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
items.summary: Showed bidirectional masked-language-model pretraining beats left-to-right pretraining, meaning you should reach for an encoder-only model (not a decoder-only LLM) for classification/embedding tasks

items.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
items.tldr: Splits an image into fixed patches, embeds them like tokens, and feeds them to a plain Transformer encoder -- shows that with enough pretraining data a convolution-free model matches or beats CNNs on image classification
items.key_contribution: Demonstrated that a standard Transformer applied directly to sequences of image patches (the Vision Transformer, ViT), with minimal image-specific inductive bias, matches or exceeds state-of-the-art CNNs when pretrained on large datasets, establishing the Transformer as a general architecture across modalities
items.display_name: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
items.summary: Splits an image into fixed patches, embeds them like tokens, and feeds them to a plain Transformer encoder -- shows that with enough pretraining data a convolution-free model matches or beats CNNs on image classification

items.title: The Llama 3 Herd of Models
items.tldr: Documented Meta's dense 405B-parameter Llama 3 herd as an open-weight family competitive with GPT-4 -- the reference technical report for an open-weight family, though Meta's current line has moved to Llama 4's MoE design
items.key_contribution: Documented that a dense (non-MoE) Transformer scaled to 405B parameters, trained with a heavy emphasis on data quality and a straightforward training recipe rather than architectural novelty, can match leading closed frontier models like GPT-4 on a broad range of tasks while remaining fully open-weight

items.summary: Documented Meta's dense 405B-parameter Llama 3 herd as an open-weight family competitive with GPT-4 -- the reference technical report for an open-weight family, though Meta's current line has moved to Llama 4's MoE design

items.title: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization
items.tldr: Built a knowledge-graph index with hierarchical community summaries for global, holistic corpus queries -- reach for GraphRAG only for 'summarize the whole dataset' queries, given its indexing cost runs 100x-6000x that of standard vector RAG
items.key_contribution: Showed constructing an LLM-derived knowledge graph from a corpus, then generating hierarchical community summaries over that graph, enables answering global, holistic queries (e.g. 'what are the main themes across this entire dataset') that standard retrieve-then-generate RAG structurally cannot answer well
items.display_name: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization

items.title: RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation
items.tldr: Defined reference-free metrics (faithfulness, answer relevance, context relevance) for evaluating RAG pipelines with no human-labeled ground truth -- use RAGAS-style metrics as your default RAG evaluation approach rather than building bespoke evaluation
items.key_contribution: Defined a set of reference-free evaluation metrics -- faithfulness, answer relevance, and context relevance -- that assess RAG pipeline quality using only the retrieved context, the generated answer, and the query itself, without requiring human-labeled ground-truth answers
items.display_name: RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation
items.summary: Defined reference-free metrics (faithfulness, answer relevance, context relevance) for evaluating RAG pipelines with no human-labeled ground truth -- use RAGAS-style metrics as your default RAG evaluation approach rather than building bespoke evaluation

items.title: KTO: Model Alignment as Prospect Theoretic Optimization
items.tldr: Aligns models from a single binary 'good/bad' label per example instead of pairwise preferences, using a human-aware loss inspired by prospect theory -- removes the need to collect matched preferred/rejected pairs
items.key_contribution: KTO (Kahneman-Tversky Optimization), an alignment objective that learns from unpaired binary desirable/undesirable labels using a prospect-theory-inspired utility, matching or beating DPO while dropping the requirement for paired preference data that is expensive to collect
items.display_name: KTO: Model Alignment as Prospect Theoretic Optimization
items.summary: Aligns models from a single binary 'good/bad' label per example instead of pairwise preferences, using a human-aware loss inspired by prospect theory -- removes the need to collect matched preferred/rejected pairs

items.title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity
items.tldr: Simplified mixture-of-experts to top-1 routing (one expert per token), showing sparse models reach the same quality as dense ones up to 7× faster per FLOP — the recipe that made MoE the standard architecture for frontier-scale efficiency
items.key_contribution: Proved that MoE routing can be radically simple: route each token to a single expert, stabilize with an auxiliary load-balancing loss, selective float32 in the router, and expert dropout — decoupling parameter count from per-token compute and setting the template DeepSeek-V3, Mixtral, and frontier MoEs elaborate
items.display_name: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity
items.summary: Simplified mixture-of-experts to top-1 routing (one expert per token), showing sparse models reach the same quality as dense ones up to 7× faster per FLOP — the recipe that made MoE the standard architecture for frontier-scale efficiency

items.title: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers
items.tldr: Showed one-shot post-training quantization to 3-4 bits is feasible for 100B+ param models in hours with minimal accuracy loss -- reach for GPTQ (or AWQ) as a default quantization option before more disruptive approaches
items.key_contribution: Demonstrated a layer-wise post-training quantization method using approximate second-order (Hessian) information that compresses generative Transformers to 3-4 bits per weight, running on models with hundreds of billions of parameters in a few GPU-hours, without significant accuracy loss
items.display_name: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers
items.summary: Showed one-shot post-training quantization to 3-4 bits is feasible for 100B+ param models in hours with minimal accuracy loss -- reach for GPTQ (or AWQ) as a default quantization option before more disruptive approaches

items.title: Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels
items.tldr: Showed you can retrieve well in a zero-shot setting by generating a hypothetical answer first and embedding that instead of the raw query, meaning you should reach for HyDE specifically when you have no labeled relevance data to train or fine-tune a retriever
items.key_contribution: Showed that generating a 'fake' hypothetical document from the query with an instruction-following LLM, then embedding that hypothetical document (not the raw query) for similarity search, significantly outperforms unsupervised dense retrieval baselines with zero relevance-labeled training data
items.display_name: Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels
items.summary: Showed you can retrieve well in a zero-shot setting by generating a hypothetical answer first and embedding that instead of the raw query, meaning you should reach for HyDE specifically when you have no labeled relevance data to train or fine-tune a retriever

items.key_contribution: Established the Naive → Advanced → Modular RAG progression as the field's shared taxonomy, decomposing the space into pre-retrieval (query rewriting, routing), retrieval (embedding choice, chunking), post-retrieval (reranking, compression), and generation stages, plus an evaluation-framework synthesis

items.tldr: Open-weight, natively multimodal model family (2.3B-31B, dense + MoE) with a thinking mode and an encoder-free 12B that ingests raw audio and image patches -- the strongest open-weight option at small/mid scale as of mid-2026
items.key_contribution: A new generation of open-weight natively multimodal models spanning 2.3B-31B parameters with dense and Mixture-of-Experts variants, integrated thinking mode, improved long-context and inference efficiency, and a unified encoder-free architecture for the 12B model that consumes raw audio and image patches directly

items.title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
items.tldr: Introduced selective state-space models with input-dependent dynamics and a hardware-aware parallel scan, achieving Transformer-quality language modeling with linear-time inference — the strongest attention alternative, now shipping in hybrid production models
items.key_contribution: Made SSM parameters input-dependent (selective), sacrificing convolutional training form but recovering efficiency with a hardware-aware parallel scan — closing the quality gap between state-space models and Transformers on language while keeping O(1) per-token inference state

items.title: Textbooks Are All You Need
items.tldr: The phi-1 paper: a 1.3B model trained on 7B tokens of filtered 'textbook-quality' and synthetic data hit 50.6% HumanEval — the flagship argument that data quality can substitute for orders of magnitude of scale, launching the small-language-model program
items.key_contribution: Demonstrated that aggressive quality filtering (LLM-classifier-selected web code) plus GPT-generated synthetic textbooks and exercises lets a 1.3B model rival much larger code models — establishing data curation and synthetic data as first-class alternatives to parameter scaling
items.display_name: Textbooks Are All You Need
