items.title: REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training
items.tldr: First model to pretrain a language model jointly with a learned neural retriever over Wikipedia, backpropagating through retrieval — establishing that external knowledge can be a trained component of an LM rather than a bolt-on
items.key_contribution: Made retrieval differentiable and part of the pretraining objective: a latent-variable formulation where the retriever's document distribution is trained end-to-end via masked-language-modeling signal, with asynchronous MIPS index refreshes — the founding architecture of learned retrieval augmentation
items.display_name: REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training
items.summary: First model to pretrain a language model jointly with a learned neural retriever over Wikipedia, backpropagating through retrieval — establishing that external knowledge can be a trained component of an LM rather than a bolt-on

items.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
items.tldr: Introduced residual connections (skip connections) that let networks learn residual functions relative to the identity, making very deep networks trainable and unblocking the depth scaling that later architectures — including Transformers — depend on
items.key_contribution: Reframed each layer block to learn a residual F(x) added back to its input x, so gradients flow through identity shortcuts; this fixed the degradation problem that had made naively-deeper networks train worse, enabling 100+ layer networks
items.display_name: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
items.summary: Introduced residual connections (skip connections) that let networks learn residual functions relative to the identity, making very deep networks trainable and unblocking the depth scaling that later architectures — including Transformers — depend on

items.title: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models
items.tldr: HELM established a reproducible evaluation framework that compares language models across scenarios and multiple quality, robustness, fairness, and efficiency metrics rather than relying on one accuracy leaderboard.
items.key_contribution: The paper introduced a scenario-and-metric evaluation matrix with standardized model adapters, shared prompts, and transparent reports so model comparisons include calibration, robustness, fairness, bias, toxicity, and efficiency alongside accuracy.
items.display_name: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models
items.summary: HELM established a reproducible evaluation framework that compares language models across scenarios and multiple quality, robustness, fairness, and efficiency metrics rather than relying on one accuracy leaderboard.

items.title: Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding
items.tldr: Introduced MMLU: 57-subject multiple-choice knowledge exam that became the field's default capability number for half a decade — now saturated and largely superseded (MMLU-Pro, GPQA), but still the single most-cited benchmark score in model cards
items.key_contribution: Built a 15,908-question, 57-subject benchmark spanning STEM, humanities, law, and medicine to measure pretraining-acquired knowledge in zero/few-shot settings — establishing both the benchmark that anchored model comparison through the GPT-4 era and the now-standard practice of reporting broad multitask accuracy
items.display_name: Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding
items.summary: Introduced MMLU: 57-subject multiple-choice knowledge exam that became the field's default capability number for half a decade — now saturated and largely superseded (MMLU-Pro, GPQA), but still the single most-cited benchmark score in model cards

items.title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
items.tldr: Introduced knowledge distillation — training a small 'student' model to match the soft output distribution of a large 'teacher' — the basis for compressing large models into cheap, fast ones for deployment
items.key_contribution: Showed a teacher's softened probabilities (logits divided by a temperature) carry 'dark knowledge' about class similarities that lets a much smaller student learn better than training on hard labels alone
items.display_name: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
items.summary: Introduced knowledge distillation — training a small 'student' model to match the soft output distribution of a large 'teacher' — the basis for compressing large models into cheap, fast ones for deployment

items.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
items.tldr: Made diffusion models practical for high-quality image generation by training a network to reverse a gradual noising process, establishing the denoising-diffusion recipe behind modern image and video generators
items.key_contribution: Connected diffusion probabilistic models to denoising score matching and showed a simple reweighted training objective (predict the added noise) produces high-fidelity samples, turning diffusion into a competitive generative paradigm
items.display_name: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
items.summary: Made diffusion models practical for high-quality image generation by training a network to reverse a gradual noising process, establishing the denoising-diffusion recipe behind modern image and video generators

items.title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
items.tldr: The Chinchilla paper: showed contemporary LLMs were dramatically undertrained — compute-optimal training scales parameters and data equally (~20 tokens per parameter), and a 70B model trained on 1.4T tokens beat a 280B model — resetting how the field allocates training compute
items.key_contribution: Corrected Kaplan et al.'s scaling laws with better-controlled experiments (varying LR schedules with token budgets), finding N and D should scale in equal proportion — 'Chinchilla-optimal' ~20 tokens/parameter — and validated it by training Chinchilla-70B to outperform the 4x-larger Gopher-280B at equal compute
items.display_name: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
items.summary: The Chinchilla paper: showed contemporary LLMs were dramatically undertrained — compute-optimal training scales parameters and data equally (~20 tokens per parameter), and a 70B model trained on 1.4T tokens beat a 280B model — resetting how the field allocates training compute

items.title: ORPO: Monolithic Preference Optimization without Reference Model
items.tldr: Folds preference alignment into supervised fine-tuning in a single stage by adding an odds-ratio penalty to the SFT loss — no separate reference model and no separate DPO/RLHF phase, cutting alignment to one training run.
items.key_contribution: Showed that a small odds-ratio-based penalty appended to the standard SFT cross-entropy loss suffices to align a base model to preferences in one monolithic stage — removing both the reference model and the separate preference-optimization phase that SFT-then-DPO/RLHF pipelines require.
items.display_name: ORPO: Monolithic Preference Optimization without Reference Model
items.summary: Folds preference alignment into supervised fine-tuning in a single stage by adding an odds-ratio penalty to the SFT loss — no separate reference model and no separate DPO/RLHF phase, cutting alignment to one training run.

items.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
items.tldr: Showed you can fine-tune a large model by training only small low-rank update matrices injected into attention weights, meaning you should use LoRA (not full fine-tuning) whenever GPU memory or storage for many fine-tuned variants is a constraint
items.key_contribution: Demonstrated that the weight update needed to adapt a pretrained model to a new task has a low intrinsic rank, so training two small low-rank matrices per layer (instead of the full weight matrix) achieves comparable task performance at a fraction of the trainable-parameter count
items.display_name: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
items.summary: Showed you can fine-tune a large model by training only small low-rank update matrices injected into attention weights, meaning you should use LoRA (not full fine-tuning) whenever GPU memory or storage for many fine-tuned variants is a constraint

items.title: A Survey on Hallucination in Large Language Models: Principles, Taxonomy, Challenges, and Open Questions
items.tldr: The reference taxonomy for hallucination: splits it into factuality vs faithfulness, traces causes through data, training, and inference, and catalogs detection benchmarks and mitigation strategies — the structured map behind grounding and guardrail engineering
items.key_contribution: Defined the now-standard factuality-hallucination (output contradicts or fabricates world knowledge) versus faithfulness-hallucination (output contradicts provided context or instructions) distinction, with a causal analysis spanning data, training, and inference stages and a systematic review of detection benchmarks and mitigations per cause
items.display_name: A Survey on Hallucination in Large Language Models: Principles, Taxonomy, Challenges, and Open Questions
items.summary: The reference taxonomy for hallucination: splits it into factuality vs faithfulness, traces causes through data, training, and inference, and catalogs detection benchmarks and mitigation strategies — the structured map behind grounding and guardrail engineering

items.title: Regression Accumulation in Multi-Turn LLM Programming Conversations
items.tldr: Shows that later coding-agent turns can break earlier requirements and evaluates a verification gate that retests prior behavior before accepting a change.
items.key_contribution: Turns HumanEval+ and MBPP+ tasks into eight-turn requirement-evolution chains, measuring regression preservation across 26,016 model-turn instances instead of only final-turn correctness.
items.display_name: Regression Accumulation in Multi-Turn LLM Programming Conversations
items.summary: Shows that later coding-agent turns can break earlier requirements and evaluates a verification gate that retests prior behavior before accepting a change.

items.title: Meta-Benchmarks for Financial-Services LLM Evaluation
items.tldr: A weighting scheme that scores 288 models on banking work activities by Elo, down-weighting benchmarks that no longer separate leaders.
items.key_contribution: A three-factor multiplicative weight makes benchmark retirement automatic instead of editorial, which keeps the scorecard current without a committee.
items.display_name: Meta-Benchmarks for Financial-Services LLM Evaluation
items.summary: A weighting scheme that scores 288 models on banking work activities by Elo, down-weighting benchmarks that no longer separate leaders.

items.title: Leveraging Passage Retrieval with Generative Models for Open Domain Question Answering (Fusion-in-Decoder)
items.tldr: Fusion-in-Decoder: encode each retrieved passage independently, concatenate the encodings, and let the decoder attend across all of them — scaling QA accuracy monotonically with passage count at linear (not quadratic) encoding cost
items.key_contribution: Showed that the winning way to combine many retrieved passages is architectural, not selective: independent encoding + joint decoder attention lets a T5 reader aggregate evidence from 100 passages, beating RAG and extractive readers and revealing that accuracy keeps climbing as you add passages
items.display_name: Leveraging Passage Retrieval with Generative Models for Open Domain Question Answering (Fusion-in-Decoder)
items.summary: Fusion-in-Decoder: encode each retrieved passage independently, concatenate the encodings, and let the decoder attend across all of them — scaling QA accuracy monotonically with passage count at linear (not quadratic) encoding cost

items.title: Unsupervised Dense Information Retrieval with Contrastive Learning (Contriever)
items.tldr: Trained a competitive dense retriever with no labeled query-document pairs, using contrastive learning over automatically-constructed positive pairs — strong zero-shot retrieval and a much better fine-tuning starting point than BM25 or random init.
items.key_contribution: Showed dense retrievers can be pretrained purely unsupervised via contrastive learning (independent cropping / inverse cloze-style positives, MoCo-style negatives), matching or beating BM25 zero-shot and transferring well across domains — removing the labeled-data bottleneck that had made dense retrieval brittle out-of-domain.
items.display_name: Unsupervised Dense Information Retrieval with Contrastive Learning (Contriever)
items.summary: Trained a competitive dense retriever with no labeled query-document pairs, using contrastive learning over automatically-constructed positive pairs — strong zero-shot retrieval and a much better fine-tuning starting point than BM25 or random init.

items.title: Memory is Reconstructed, Not Retrieved: Graph Memory for LLM Agents
items.tldr: Replaces static retrieve-then-reason agent memory with active reconstruction over a Cue-Tag-Content graph -- the agent iteratively explores and prunes retrieval paths as evidence accumulates, gaining up to 23% on LoCoMo/LongMemEval while cutting tokens
items.key_contribution: MRAgent: an associative Cue-Tag-Content memory graph plus an active reconstruction mechanism that integrates LLM reasoning into memory access itself, letting the agent dynamically adapt retrieval paths to intermediate evidence instead of executing a fixed retrieve-then-reason pipeline
items.display_name: Memory is Reconstructed, Not Retrieved: Graph Memory for LLM Agents
items.summary: Replaces static retrieve-then-reason agent memory with active reconstruction over a Cue-Tag-Content graph -- the agent iteratively explores and prunes retrieval paths as evidence accumulates, gaining up to 23% on LoCoMo/LongMemEval while cutting tokens

items.title: Mixtral of Experts
items.tldr: Proved sparse mixture-of-experts works at open-weights scale: Mixtral 8x7B matched or beat Llama 2 70B while activating only 13B parameters per token, making MoE the default architecture for efficient frontier models
items.key_contribution: Demonstrated a production-quality sparse MoE decoder (8 experts, top-2 routing per layer) whose open release validated that MoE delivers dense-model quality at a fraction of inference FLOPs — the architectural template most subsequent open frontier models (DeepSeek-V3, Qwen3-MoE, Kimi K2, GLM-4.5) adopted and extended
items.display_name: Mixtral of Experts
items.summary: Proved sparse mixture-of-experts works at open-weights scale: Mixtral 8x7B matched or beat Llama 2 70B while activating only 13B parameters per token, making MoE the default architecture for efficient frontier models

items.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
items.tldr: SWE-bench: 2,294 real GitHub issues from 12 Python repos, graded by running the repos' own tests against model-generated patches — the benchmark that replaced toy coding problems and became the scoreboard of the coding-agent era
items.key_contribution: Built the first execution-graded benchmark of real-world software engineering — resolve an actual issue in a full repository, judged by the project's real test suite — exposing how far models were from practical SWE (sub-2% at release) and defining the metric coding agents now compete on
items.display_name: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
items.summary: SWE-bench: 2,294 real GitHub issues from 12 Python repos, graded by running the repos' own tests against model-generated patches — the benchmark that replaced toy coding problems and became the scoreboard of the coding-agent era

items.title: Billion-scale similarity search with GPUs
items.tldr: The FAISS paper — GPU-accelerated similarity search with product quantization that made billion-vector nearest-neighbor search practical, underpinning large-scale retrieval and vector-store backends
items.key_contribution: GPU-optimized k-selection and inverted-file + product-quantization (IVF-PQ) indexes that compress vectors and search them at scale, trading a controllable amount of recall for order-of-magnitude memory and speed gains
items.display_name: Billion-scale similarity search with GPUs
items.summary: The FAISS paper — GPU-accelerated similarity search with product quantization that made billion-vector nearest-neighbor search practical, underpinning large-scale retrieval and vector-store backends

items.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
items.tldr: Established that language-model loss falls as smooth power laws in parameters, data, and compute across many orders of magnitude — the empirical foundation of the scaling era — though its specific compute-optimal allocation was later corrected by Chinchilla
items.key_contribution: First systematic demonstration that LM cross-entropy loss scales as predictable power laws in N (parameters), D (data), and C (compute), with performance depending weakly on architecture within the transformer family — turning model development into an extrapolation problem and directly motivating GPT-3
items.display_name: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
items.summary: Established that language-model loss falls as smooth power laws in parameters, data, and compute across many orders of magnitude — the empirical foundation of the scaling era — though its specific compute-optimal allocation was later corrected by Chinchilla

items.title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
items.tldr: Showed a simple dual-encoder trained with in-batch negatives beats BM25 for passage retrieval — the paper that made dense embedding retrieval the default, and the direct ancestor of every embedding model powering today's RAG stacks
items.key_contribution: Demonstrated that dense retrieval (two BERT encoders, dot-product similarity, contrastive training with in-batch and hard BM25 negatives) outperforms sparse lexical retrieval by 9-19% top-20 accuracy with only thousands of training pairs — establishing the dual-encoder + vector-index pattern all modern RAG retrieval uses
items.display_name: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
items.summary: Showed a simple dual-encoder trained with in-batch negatives beats BM25 for passage retrieval — the paper that made dense embedding retrieval the default, and the direct ancestor of every embedding model powering today's RAG stacks

items.title: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT
items.tldr: Introduced late interaction: keep one vector per token and score via MaxSim at query time, capturing term-level matching that single-vector retrieval loses — the architecture behind ColBERTv2/PLAID and modern multi-vector rerankers
items.key_contribution: Late interaction — encoding queries and documents into per-token embedding bags scored by sum-of-MaxSim — retaining cross-encoder-like term-level expressiveness while preserving the offline-indexable efficiency of bi-encoders; the third point (with bi- and cross-encoders) on the retrieval quality/cost frontier
items.display_name: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT
items.summary: Introduced late interaction: keep one vector per token and score via MaxSim at query time, capturing term-level matching that single-vector retrieval loses — the architecture behind ColBERTv2/PLAID and modern multi-vector rerankers

items.title: Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners
items.tldr: Appending the single trigger phrase 'Let's think step by step' elicits chain-of-thought reasoning zero-shot — no exemplars needed — showing that reasoning behavior in LLMs is latent and can be unlocked by prompt format alone
items.key_contribution: Demonstrated that chain-of-thought reasoning does not require few-shot exemplars: a two-stage prompt (reasoning trigger, then answer extraction) lifts InstructGPT from 17.7% to 78.7% on MultiArith zero-shot, establishing that CoT is a decodable latent capability rather than in-context imitation
items.display_name: Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners
items.summary: Appending the single trigger phrase 'Let's think step by step' elicits chain-of-thought reasoning zero-shot — no exemplars needed — showing that reasoning behavior in LLMs is latent and can be unlocked by prompt format alone

items.title: Evaluating Chunking Strategies for Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Academic Texts
items.tldr: A negative result: cluster-based semantic chunking did not beat fixed-size or recursive chunking on long academic theses.
items.key_contribution: Tests a widely held assumption against two simpler baselines rather than against a strawman, which is the comparison most teams skip.
items.display_name: Evaluating Chunking Strategies for Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Academic Texts
items.summary: A negative result: cluster-based semantic chunking did not beat fixed-size or recursive chunking on long academic theses.

items.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
items.tldr: Applied OS virtual-memory paging to the KV cache: non-contiguous fixed-size blocks eliminate the 60-80% memory waste of contiguous allocation, enabling 2-4x serving throughput — this is the vLLM paper, and paged KV caches are now universal
items.key_contribution: Diagnosed that contiguous KV-cache allocation wastes 60-80% of memory to fragmentation and over-reservation, and introduced PagedAttention — block-based virtual KV memory with a block table per sequence, enabling near-zero waste, prefix sharing via copy-on-write, and 2-4x throughput; shipped as vLLM
items.display_name: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
items.summary: Applied OS virtual-memory paging to the KV cache: non-contiguous fixed-size blocks eliminate the 60-80% memory waste of contiguous allocation, enabling 2-4x serving throughput — this is the vLLM paper, and paged KV caches are now universal

items.title: Benchmarking Code Improvement with Progressive, Adaptive, and Interactive Feedback
items.tldr: A repair benchmark that scores feedback-guided code improvement on trajectories rather than a single pass/fail verdict.
items.key_contribution: The two orthogonal controls separate what the feedback points at from how much it reveals, which is the confound that makes binary repair scores uninterpretable.
items.display_name: Benchmarking Code Improvement with Progressive, Adaptive, and Interactive Feedback
items.summary: A repair benchmark that scores feedback-guided code improvement on trajectories rather than a single pass/fail verdict.

items.title: RLAIF vs. RLHF: Scaling Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback with AI Feedback
items.tldr: Showed that preference labels generated by an off-the-shelf LLM (RLAIF) can match human-labeled RLHF on summarization and dialogue, and that policies can even be trained directly against LLM-assigned rewards — making preference alignment far cheaper to scale.
items.key_contribution: Provided a systematic head-to-head showing AI-generated preference feedback yields alignment quality comparable to human feedback across several tasks, introduced 'direct RLAIF' (skip the reward model and score with the LLM online), and analyzed prompting choices that make the AI labeler reliable — reducing alignment's dependence on costly human annotation.
items.display_name: RLAIF vs. RLHF: Scaling Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback with AI Feedback
items.summary: Showed that preference labels generated by an off-the-shelf LLM (RLAIF) can match human-labeled RLHF on summarization and dialogue, and that policies can even be trained directly against LLM-assigned rewards — making preference alignment far cheaper to scale.

items.title: The Power of Scale for Parameter-Efficient Prompt Tuning
items.tldr: Showed you can adapt a frozen LLM to a task by learning only a small set of continuous 'soft prompt' vectors, and that this matches full fine-tuning as model scale grows — an early parameter-efficient tuning method
items.key_contribution: Introduced prompt tuning: prepend trainable continuous embeddings to the input and train only those, keeping all model weights frozen; demonstrated it closes the gap with full fine-tuning at large scale
items.display_name: The Power of Scale for Parameter-Efficient Prompt Tuning
items.summary: Showed you can adapt a frozen LLM to a task by learning only a small set of continuous 'soft prompt' vectors, and that this matches full fine-tuning as model scale grows — an early parameter-efficient tuning method

items.title: Do You Need a Frontier Model as a Citation Verifier? Benchmarking Rubric LLMs for Deep-Research Source Attribution
items.tldr: Compares eight LLM judges on deep-research citation attribution and shows why aggregate F1 is insufficient for controlling verifier bias.
items.key_contribution: Separates source relevance from factual support across 1,248 rubric decisions and exposes judge-specific false-positive and false-negative tendencies that can distort a reward or acceptance loop.
items.display_name: Do You Need a Frontier Model as a Citation Verifier? Benchmarking Rubric LLMs for Deep-Research Source Attribution
items.summary: Compares eight LLM judges on deep-research citation attribution and shows why aggregate F1 is insufficient for controlling verifier bias.

items.title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding
items.tldr: Showed a small draft model's guesses can be verified in parallel by the full model with zero change to the output distribution, meaning production inference engines should implement speculative decoding to cut generation latency without sacrificing exactness
items.key_contribution: Demonstrated that a smaller, faster 'approximation' model can generate candidate tokens which the larger target model verifies in a single parallel forward pass, producing 2-3x generation speedups while provably preserving the target model's exact output distribution
items.display_name: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding
items.summary: Showed a small draft model's guesses can be verified in parallel by the full model with zero change to the output distribution, meaning production inference engines should implement speculative decoding to cut generation latency without sacrificing exactness

items.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
items.tldr: Coined 'RAG': a jointly-trained retriever plus generator beats closed-book generation on knowledge-intensive tasks -- ground generation in retrieved documents, though production RAG today uses a simpler decoupled pipeline
items.key_contribution: Established the term and general framing of retrieval-augmented generation: combining a pretrained parametric seq2seq model with a non-parametric dense vector index that can be updated without retraining the generator
items.display_name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
items.summary: Coined 'RAG': a jointly-trained retriever plus generator beats closed-book generation on knowledge-intensive tasks -- ground generation in retrieved documents, though production RAG today uses a simpler decoupled pipeline

items.title: BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models
items.tldr: Connected a frozen image encoder to a frozen LLM with a small trainable Querying Transformer (Q-Former), two-stage trained — reaching strong VQA/captioning with a tiny fraction of trainable parameters, the efficient bridge pattern behind many open VLMs.
items.key_contribution: Introduced the Q-Former: a lightweight transformer with learned query tokens that extracts a fixed set of language-aligned visual features from a frozen image encoder and feeds them to a frozen LLM, trained in two stages (representation learning then generative), achieving VLM capability while training only ~1% of the parameters.
items.display_name: BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models
items.summary: Connected a frozen image encoder to a frozen LLM with a small trainable Querying Transformer (Q-Former), two-stage trained — reaching strong VQA/captioning with a tiny fraction of trainable parameters, the efficient bridge pattern behind many open VLMs.

items.title: ADR: An Agentic Detection System for Enterprise Agentic AI Security
items.tldr: Describes an enterprise agent-security detection and response system combining high-fidelity telemetry, red-team exploration, and two-tier online detection.
items.key_contribution: Combines an ADR Sensor, Explorer, and Detector, then evaluates the system on ADR-Bench and AgentDojo while reporting deployment experience and explicitly scoped claims.
items.display_name: ADR: An Agentic Detection System for Enterprise Agentic AI Security
items.summary: Describes an enterprise agent-security detection and response system combining high-fidelity telemetry, red-team exploration, and two-tier online detection.

items.title: Dual-Confidence Contrastive Decoding for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.tldr: Uses document- and token-level confidence to suppress conflicting retrieved evidence during training-free RAG decoding.
items.key_contribution: Introduces DCCD and the DRQA conflict benchmark, targeting disagreement among retrieved documents rather than only conflict between model memory and retrieved context.
items.display_name: Dual-Confidence Contrastive Decoding for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.summary: Uses document- and token-level confidence to suppress conflicting retrieved evidence during training-free RAG decoding.

items.title: The Mirage of Optimizing Training Policies: Monotonic Inference Policies as the Real Objective for LLM Reinforcement Learning
items.tldr: LLM RL optimizes the training-engine policy, but you deploy the inference-engine policy -- and the two disagree on trajectory probabilities even with synced weights. Proposes MIPI/MIPU to make the deployed policy the optimization objective
items.key_contribution: Identifies an objective misalignment underlying training-inference mismatch in LLM RL -- improving the training-engine policy does not necessarily improve the inference-engine policy actually deployed -- and proposes Monotonic Inference Policy Improvement (MIPI) with a two-step update framework (MIPU) that targets the inference policy directly
items.display_name: The Mirage of Optimizing Training Policies: Monotonic Inference Policies as the Real Objective for LLM Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: LLM RL optimizes the training-engine policy, but you deploy the inference-engine policy -- and the two disagree on trajectory probabilities even with synced weights. Proposes MIPI/MIPU to make the deployed policy the optimization objective

items.title: TruthfulQA: Measuring How Models Mimic Human Falsehoods
items.tldr: A benchmark of questions engineered to trigger common human misconceptions, revealing that larger models can be *less* truthful because they better imitate popular false beliefs in their training data -- truthfulness is not a free byproduct of scale
items.key_contribution: A 817-question adversarial benchmark spanning many categories designed so that imitating training-text patterns yields false answers, empirically demonstrating inverse scaling on truthfulness and providing an evaluation (with automated 'GPT-judge' scoring) for the imitative-falsehood failure mode
items.display_name: TruthfulQA: Measuring How Models Mimic Human Falsehoods
items.summary: A benchmark of questions engineered to trigger common human misconceptions, revealing that larger models can be *less* truthful because they better imitate popular false beliefs in their training data -- truthfulness is not a free byproduct of scale

items.title: AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration
items.tldr: Showed ~1% of weight channels are 'salient' — identified by activation magnitudes, not weight values — and protecting them via per-channel scaling enables accurate 4-bit weight quantization without backpropagation; AWQ is now a standard deployment format
items.key_contribution: Activation-aware saliency: scaling up the ~1% of weight channels with large activation magnitudes before 4-bit quantization preserves accuracy without any gradient-based reconstruction, generalizing better than GPTQ's Hessian-based approach (especially for instruction-tuned and multimodal models) and shipping with efficient kernels (TinyChat)
items.display_name: AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration
items.summary: Showed ~1% of weight channels are 'salient' — identified by activation magnitudes, not weight values — and protecting them via per-channel scaling enables accurate 4-bit weight quantization without backpropagation; AWQ is now a standard deployment format

items.title: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach
items.tldr: Shows BERT was significantly undertrained: with more data, longer training, bigger batches, no next-sentence-prediction, and dynamic masking, the same architecture reaches much higher scores -- a lesson that training recipe often matters more than architecture
items.key_contribution: A rigorous replication study of BERT establishing that pretraining design choices (data size, training duration, batch size, removing next-sentence prediction, dynamic masking) were the real bottleneck, producing a substantially stronger encoder from an unchanged architecture and setting the standard MLM recipe used since
items.display_name: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach
items.summary: Shows BERT was significantly undertrained: with more data, longer training, bigger batches, no next-sentence-prediction, and dynamic masking, the same architecture reaches much higher scores -- a lesson that training recipe often matters more than architecture

items.title: Visual Instruction Tuning (LLaVA)
items.tldr: Connected a frozen CLIP vision encoder to a LLaMA-family LLM with just a linear projection, trained on GPT-4-generated visual instruction data — establishing the minimal recipe (encoder + projector + LLM) behind most open vision-language models
items.key_contribution: Two firsts that became defaults: machine-generating multimodal instruction-following data by prompting text-only GPT-4 with image captions/boxes, and showing a trivially simple projector suffices to graft vision onto a pretrained LLM — GPT-4V-style assistant behavior from academic-scale compute
items.display_name: Visual Instruction Tuning (LLaVA)
items.summary: Connected a frozen CLIP vision encoder to a LLaMA-family LLM with just a linear projection, trained on GPT-4-generated visual instruction data — establishing the minimal recipe (encoder + projector + LLM) behind most open vision-language models

items.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
authors: et al. (Stanford / UC Berkeley / Samaya AI)
items.tldr: Documented the U-shaped curve: LLMs use information at the beginning and end of long contexts far better than the middle — sometimes scoring worse with relevant context mid-prompt than with no context at all — the finding that shaped RAG context-ordering practice
items.key_contribution: First systematic characterization of positional bias in long-context use: controlled experiments moving the answer-bearing document through the context show robust U-shaped performance across models, proving that a long context window is not the same as effective context use
items.display_name: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
items.summary: Documented the U-shaped curve: LLMs use information at the beginning and end of long contexts far better than the middle — sometimes scoring worse with relevant context mid-prompt than with no context at all — the finding that shaped RAG context-ordering practice

items.title: From Tool Connection to Execution Control: Benchmarking Security Invariants in MCP-Style Agent Runtimes
items.tldr: Argues that MCP-style connection conventions need an explicit execution-control layer with principals, capabilities, data-flow checks, and deny-path audit.
items.key_contribution: Defines eight execution invariants and evaluates a Handle-Capability Protocol runtime against a naive connection layer and a mitigation baseline across ten modeled attack cases.
items.display_name: From Tool Connection to Execution Control: Benchmarking Security Invariants in MCP-Style Agent Runtimes
items.summary: Argues that MCP-style connection conventions need an explicit execution-control layer with principals, capabilities, data-flow checks, and deny-path audit.

items.title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
items.tldr: Showed self-critique-then-revise loops can improve output quality, but later rigorous studies found weak initial-response prompts inflated the reported improvement -- treat this with caution, not as a validated default
items.key_contribution: Proposed an iterative loop where a model generates output, critiques its own output, and revises based on that self-critique, with no additional training and no external feedback signal, reporting quality improvements across several generation tasks
items.display_name: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
items.summary: Showed self-critique-then-revise loops can improve output quality, but later rigorous studies found weak initial-response prompts inflated the reported improvement -- treat this with caution, not as a validated default

items.title: Efficient and robust approximate nearest neighbor search using Hierarchical Navigable Small World graphs
items.tldr: Introduced the HNSW graph index for approximate nearest-neighbor search — the algorithm powering most production vector databases and the retrieval step of essentially every RAG system
items.key_contribution: A multi-layer navigable small-world graph that gives logarithmic-scaling search with high recall, making billion-scale similarity search fast enough for real-time retrieval
items.display_name: Efficient and robust approximate nearest neighbor search using Hierarchical Navigable Small World graphs
items.summary: Introduced the HNSW graph index for approximate nearest-neighbor search — the algorithm powering most production vector databases and the retrieval step of essentially every RAG system

items.title: AgentAtlas: Beyond Outcome Leaderboards for LLM Agents
items.tldr: Provides a diagnostic vocabulary for separating agent outcomes, control decisions, trajectory failures, and benchmark coverage instead of relying on one success score.
items.key_contribution: Defines six control-decision states, a trajectory-failure vocabulary, and a 0/1/2 coverage audit over fifteen agent benchmarks; its 1,342-item demonstration is explicitly illustrative rather than a public leaderboard.
items.display_name: AgentAtlas: Beyond Outcome Leaderboards for LLM Agents
items.summary: Provides a diagnostic vocabulary for separating agent outcomes, control decisions, trajectory failures, and benchmark coverage instead of relying on one success score.

items.title: SimPO: Simple Preference Optimization with a Reference-Free Reward
items.tldr: A preference-optimization objective that drops DPO's reference model, using the average log-probability of a response as an implicit reward plus a target margin — simpler, cheaper (no reference forward pass), and often stronger than DPO.
items.key_contribution: Showed you can align to preferences without a reference model by using length-normalized average log-likelihood as the implicit reward and adding a target reward margin, aligning the training objective with the generation metric — matching or beating DPO while halving memory/compute per step.
items.display_name: SimPO: Simple Preference Optimization with a Reference-Free Reward
items.summary: A preference-optimization objective that drops DPO's reference model, using the average log-probability of a response as an implicit reward plus a target margin — simpler, cheaper (no reference forward pass), and often stronger than DPO.

items.title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space (word2vec)
items.tldr: Introduced CBOW and skip-gram, shallow models that learn dense word vectors from raw text cheaply enough to scale to billions of words — establishing that meaning can be captured as geometry (king − man + woman ≈ queen) and seeding the entire embedding era.
items.key_contribution: Showed that a shallow, log-linear objective (predict context from word or vice versa) yields word vectors encoding rich semantic and syntactic regularities as linear offsets, trainable orders of magnitude faster than prior neural LMs — making learned embeddings a practical default input representation for NLP.
items.display_name: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space (word2vec)
items.summary: Introduced CBOW and skip-gram, shallow models that learn dense word vectors from raw text cheaply enough to scale to billions of words — establishing that meaning can be captured as geometry (king − man + woman ≈ queen) and seeding the entire embedding era.

items.title: Retrieval as Reasoning: Self-Evolving Agent-Native Retrieval via LLM-Wiki
items.tldr: Recasts agent retrieval as search, reading, link traversal, and evidence-sufficiency decisions over a compiled, self-evolving wiki rather than flat embedding lookup.
items.key_contribution: Introduces structured wiki pages with bidirectional links, tool-calling search/read/follow operations, and an Error Book for structural and semantic correction.
items.display_name: Retrieval as Reasoning: Self-Evolving Agent-Native Retrieval via LLM-Wiki
items.summary: Recasts agent retrieval as search, reading, link traversal, and evidence-sufficiency decisions over a compiled, self-evolving wiki rather than flat embedding lookup.

items.title: MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
items.tldr: MTEB: 8 embedding task families across 58 datasets and 112 languages, with a public leaderboard — the benchmark that made embedding models comparable and whose central finding still holds: no single model wins everywhere
items.key_contribution: Unified embedding evaluation, which had been task-siloed (STS papers vs retrieval papers), into one reproducible harness spanning classification, clustering, retrieval, reranking, STS and more — establishing the leaderboard that now effectively arbitrates the embedding-model market
items.display_name: MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
items.summary: MTEB: 8 embedding task families across 58 datasets and 112 languages, with a public leaderboard — the benchmark that made embedding models comparable and whose central finding still holds: no single model wins everywhere

items.title: WebGPT: Browser-assisted question-answering with human feedback
items.tldr: Trained GPT-3 to operate a text-based web browser — searching, clicking, quoting — and answer questions with citations, using imitation learning plus human-preference RL; the first serious tool-using LLM agent and the origin of citation-grounded answers
items.key_contribution: Established the recipe for tool-using assistants before 'agents' existed as a category: represent tool use as text commands in an environment, bootstrap with human demonstrations, optimize with preference-based rejection sampling/RL — and make the model collect quoted evidence so humans can verify answers they can't fact-check themselves
items.display_name: WebGPT: Browser-assisted question-answering with human feedback
items.summary: Trained GPT-3 to operate a text-based web browser — searching, clicking, quoting — and answer questions with citations, using imitation learning plus human-preference RL; the first serious tool-using LLM agent and the origin of citation-grounded answers

items.title: NExT-GPT: Any-to-Any Multimodal LLM
items.tldr: NExT-GPT combines a language model with modality encoders and diffusion decoders so one instruction-tuned system can perceive and generate text, images, video, and audio in arbitrary combinations.
items.key_contribution: The paper presented an any-to-any multimodal architecture and a two-stage alignment and instruction-tuning recipe that connects a frozen multimodal LLM to modality-specific encoders and generation decoders through projection layers.
items.display_name: NExT-GPT: Any-to-Any Multimodal LLM
items.summary: NExT-GPT combines a language model with modality encoders and diffusion decoders so one instruction-tuned system can perceive and generate text, images, video, and audio in arbitrary combinations.

items.title: GPT-4 Technical Report
items.tldr: The GPT-4 report: human-professional-level results on real exams (top-10% bar exam), multimodal input, and loss predicted in advance from 1000x-smaller runs — while disclosing no architecture, size, or data details, setting the closed-frontier-report template
items.key_contribution: Demonstrated a capability jump to human-professional exam performance and validated predictable scaling in production (final loss forecast from much smaller runs), while establishing — for better and worse — the modern frontier-model report format: benchmarks and safety analysis without technical disclosure
items.display_name: GPT-4 Technical Report
items.summary: The GPT-4 report: human-professional-level results on real exams (top-10% bar exam), multimodal input, and loss predicted in advance from 1000x-smaller runs — while disclosing no architecture, size, or data details, setting the closed-frontier-report template

items.title: Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback
items.tldr: Established the 3-stage RLHF recipe (SFT, reward modeling, PPO) that turned GPT-3 into an assistant -- know this pipeline shape, though most teams now reach for simpler DPO instead of implementing PPO-based RLHF directly
items.key_contribution: Showed that a 1.3B-parameter model fine-tuned with human-feedback-based RLHF was preferred by human raters over the 175B-parameter base GPT-3 model, establishing that alignment technique -- not just scale -- drives usability
items.display_name: Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback
items.summary: Established the 3-stage RLHF recipe (SFT, reward modeling, PPO) that turned GPT-3 into an assistant -- know this pipeline shape, though most teams now reach for simpler DPO instead of implementing PPO-based RLHF directly

items.title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
items.tldr: Framed context-window management as an OS problem: the LLM manages its own memory hierarchy via self-editing function calls, paging information between in-context 'main memory' and external storage — the founding pattern of agent memory systems
items.key_contribution: Virtual context management — an LLM given tools to edit its own core memory, page conversation history to external storage, and retrieve on demand, with interrupts and self-directed control flow — establishing the agentic-memory design pattern that products (Letta, and memory layers generally) industrialized
items.display_name: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
items.summary: Framed context-window management as an OS problem: the LLM manages its own memory hierarchy via self-editing function calls, paging information between in-context 'main memory' and external storage — the founding pattern of agent memory systems

items.title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
items.tldr: The Smallville paper: 25 LLM agents with a memory-stream architecture (observation, retrieval by recency/importance/relevance, reflection, planning) lived in a simulated town and produced emergent social behavior — the design that defined agent memory
items.key_contribution: Introduced the memory-stream agent architecture — timestamped memories retrieved by recency, importance, and relevance, periodically synthesized into higher-level reflections that inform planning — validated by emergent multi-agent social behavior (information spreading, relationship formation, event coordination) in a 25-agent town simulation
items.display_name: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
items.summary: The Smallville paper: 25 LLM agents with a memory-stream architecture (observation, retrieval by recency/importance/relevance, reflection, planning) lived in a simulated town and produced emergent social behavior — the design that defined agent memory

items.title: Gorilla: Large Language Model Connected with Massive APIs
items.tldr: Fine-tuned an LLM to select and correctly invoke the right API from thousands of options, using retrieval of live documentation to stay current and reduce hallucinated calls — an early rigorous tool/function-calling result
items.key_contribution: Showed retrieval-aware fine-tuning on API documentation lets a model generate accurate API calls at scale and adapt to changing APIs, plus introduced APIBench and an AST-based metric for measuring call correctness and hallucination
items.display_name: Gorilla: Large Language Model Connected with Massive APIs
items.summary: Fine-tuned an LLM to select and correctly invoke the right API from thousands of options, using retrieval of live documentation to stay current and reduce hallucinated calls — an early rigorous tool/function-calling result

items.title: RWKV: Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era
items.tldr: A linear-attention RNN that trains in parallel like a Transformer but runs inference like an RNN -- O(1) memory per token and no growing KV cache, trading some expressivity for constant-cost, unbounded-context generation
items.key_contribution: An architecture combining a Transformer-style parallelizable training formulation with an RNN-style recurrent inference formulation, giving linear time and constant memory in sequence length (no KV cache), demonstrating that attention-free recurrent models can scale to billions of parameters competitively
items.display_name: RWKV: Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era
items.summary: A linear-attention RNN that trains in parallel like a Transformer but runs inference like an RNN -- O(1) memory per token and no growing KV cache, trading some expressivity for constant-cost, unbounded-context generation

items.title: Clinician-Level Agreement Without Clinical Caution: LLM Evaluator Limits in Medical AI Benchmarking
items.tldr: A German open-response clinical benchmark showing LLM judges match physician agreement while abstaining far less often.
items.key_contribution: Separates agreement from caution instead of conflating them, which is the analytical move the field most needs on judge evaluation.
items.display_name: Clinician-Level Agreement Without Clinical Caution: LLM Evaluator Limits in Medical AI Benchmarking
items.summary: A German open-response clinical benchmark showing LLM judges match physician agreement while abstaining far less often.

items.title: Validity of LLMs as Data Annotators: AMALIA on Authority
items.tldr: Tests whether agreement between the Portuguese AMALIA model and human authority annotations reflects valid construct reasoning or surface-correlated shortcuts.
items.key_contribution: Introduces a recovery-gap diagnostic that decomposes a holistic annotation prompt into theory-grounded clauses and checks whether the same construct survives recombination.
items.display_name: Validity of LLMs as Data Annotators: AMALIA on Authority
items.summary: Tests whether agreement between the Portuguese AMALIA model and human authority annotations reflects valid construct reasoning or surface-correlated shortcuts.

items.title: AGI Maze as a Benchmark Framework for World-Modeling Agents
items.tldr: A grid-maze benchmark showing LLMs do not build persistent internal world models, even with message history as memory.
items.key_contribution: Strips perception and action complexity to near zero, so a failure points at world-modelling rather than at perception or planning noise.
items.display_name: AGI Maze as a Benchmark Framework for World-Modeling Agents
items.summary: A grid-maze benchmark showing LLMs do not build persistent internal world models, even with message history as memory.

items.title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners (GPT-2)
items.tldr: Scaled a decoder-only Transformer LM to 1.5B params on WebText and showed it performs many NLP tasks zero-shot from a natural-language prompt alone — the paper that established prompting and task-agnostic pretraining as the path forward.
items.key_contribution: Demonstrated that a single large language model trained only to predict the next token can perform translation, summarization, and QA zero-shot when the task is described in the input — reframing NLP from task-specific fine-tuning to prompting a general model, and providing the first strong evidence for the scaling thesis GPT-3 later confirmed.
items.display_name: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners (GPT-2)
items.summary: Scaled a decoder-only Transformer LM to 1.5B params on WebText and showed it performs many NLP tasks zero-shot from a natural-language prompt alone — the paper that established prompting and task-agnostic pretraining as the path forward.

items.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
items.tldr: CLIP: contrastive training on 400M web image-text pairs yields a shared vision-language embedding space enabling zero-shot classification — the component that underlies multimodal LLM vision encoders, text-to-image guidance, and cross-modal retrieval
items.key_contribution: Showed natural-language supervision at web scale replaces labeled datasets for vision: a contrastive image-text objective produces zero-shot classifiers matching supervised ResNet-50 on ImageNet, and an embedding space that became the standard interface between vision and language systems
items.display_name: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
items.summary: CLIP: contrastive training on 400M web image-text pairs yields a shared vision-language embedding space enabling zero-shot classification — the component that underlies multimodal LLM vision encoders, text-to-image guidance, and cross-modal retrieval

items.title: Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision
items.tldr: Whisper: a plain encoder-decoder transformer trained on 680K hours of weakly-labeled web audio achieves human-competitive, zero-shot-robust speech recognition across 96+ languages — and its released weights became the default open ASR component
items.key_contribution: Demonstrated that scale and diversity of weak supervision beat dataset-specific training for ASR robustness: one multitask model (transcribe, translate, detect language, timestamp) generalizes zero-shot across domains where supervised models overfit their benchmarks — with fully released open weights
items.display_name: Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision
items.summary: Whisper: a plain encoder-decoder transformer trained on 680K hours of weakly-labeled web audio achieves human-competitive, zero-shot-robust speech recognition across 96+ languages — and its released weights became the default open ASR component

items.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
items.tldr: Showed the RLHF objective can be solved directly with a simple classification loss on preference pairs, with no separate reward model and no online RL -- meaning you should reach for DPO instead of implementing PPO-based RLHF for most alignment/preference-tuning work
items.key_contribution: Derived a closed-form relationship between reward functions and optimal RLHF policies, showing the standard RLHF objective can be optimized directly on preference data with a single classification-style loss, eliminating the reward-model-training and online-sampling stages of PPO-based RLHF
items.display_name: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
items.summary: Showed the RLHF objective can be solved directly with a simple classification loss on preference pairs, with no separate reward model and no online RL -- meaning you should reach for DPO instead of implementing PPO-based RLHF for most alignment/preference-tuning work

items.title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
items.tldr: The T5 paper: cast every NLP task as text-to-text, ran the field's most systematic ablation of transfer-learning choices (objectives, architectures, data, scale), and released C4 — the dataset that seeded a generation of pretraining corpora
items.key_contribution: Unified all NLP tasks under a single text-in/text-out format and empirically settled a dozen open design questions (span corruption beats other objectives; encoder-decoder competitive; scale dominates) while releasing the C4 corpus and T5 checkpoints that became standard research infrastructure
items.display_name: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
items.summary: The T5 paper: cast every NLP task as text-to-text, ran the field's most systematic ablation of transfer-learning choices (objectives, architectures, data, scale), and released C4 — the dataset that seeded a generation of pretraining corpora

items.title: Mixture-of-Depths: Dynamically Allocating Compute in Transformer-Based Language Models
items.tldr: Lets a Transformer spend different amounts of compute on different tokens by having a per-layer router send only the top-k tokens through the block and the rest skip via residual -- a compute budget set by capacity, not by every token
items.key_contribution: A method (MoD) where each layer routes a fixed capacity of tokens through its full computation while others bypass via the residual connection, giving a static compute graph with dynamic per-token depth, so the model can match baseline quality using fewer FLOPs per forward pass
items.display_name: Mixture-of-Depths: Dynamically Allocating Compute in Transformer-Based Language Models
items.summary: Lets a Transformer spend different amounts of compute on different tokens by having a per-layer router send only the top-k tokens through the block and the rest skip via residual -- a compute budget set by capacity, not by every token

items.title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks
items.tldr: Sentence-BERT: fine-tune BERT in a siamese architecture so sentences map to independently comparable embeddings — turning O(n²) cross-encoder comparison into O(n) encoding + vector similarity, and spawning the sentence-transformers library that underpins semantic search and RAG
items.key_contribution: Made transformer-quality sentence embeddings computationally practical: siamese fine-tuning with cosine-similarity objectives produces fixed vectors that cluster and search efficiently, reducing tasks like finding the most similar pair in 10K sentences from ~65 hours of BERT cross-encoding to seconds
items.display_name: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks
items.summary: Sentence-BERT: fine-tune BERT in a siamese architecture so sentences map to independently comparable embeddings — turning O(n²) cross-encoder comparison into O(n) encoding + vector similarity, and spawning the sentence-transformers library that underpins semantic search and RAG

items.title: GateMem: Benchmarking Memory Governance in Multi-Principal Shared-Memory Agents
items.tldr: Tests whether shared agent memory can provide useful long-horizon assistance without crossing principal boundaries or retaining explicitly deleted information.
items.key_contribution: Combines utility, contextual authorization, and active-forgetting tests in multi-party episodes spanning medical, office, education, and household settings.
items.display_name: GateMem: Benchmarking Memory Governance in Multi-Principal Shared-Memory Agents
items.summary: Tests whether shared agent memory can provide useful long-horizon assistance without crossing principal boundaries or retaining explicitly deleted information.

items.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
items.tldr: Ran diffusion in a compressed latent space rather than pixel space, cutting compute enough to make high-resolution, text-conditioned image generation practical — the architecture behind Stable Diffusion
items.key_contribution: Introduced a two-stage design: an autoencoder compresses images to a perceptually-equivalent latent space, and a diffusion model operates there with cross-attention conditioning, drastically reducing cost while preserving quality
items.display_name: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
items.summary: Ran diffusion in a compressed latent space rather than pixel space, cutting compute enough to make high-resolution, text-conditioned image generation practical — the architecture behind Stable Diffusion

items.title: GrepSeek: Training Search Agents for Direct Corpus Interaction
items.tldr: Trains a compact search agent to find evidence by issuing shell commands (grep-style) directly against the corpus instead of querying a vector index -- validates the index-free retrieval pattern coding agents already use, and shows how to train for it
items.key_contribution: Formalizes and optimizes direct corpus interaction (DCI): a two-stage pipeline (Tutor/Planner-generated cold-start trajectories, then GRPO refinement) that trains a compact agent to find, filter, and compose evidence from large text corpora via executable shell commands rather than a pre-built retrieval index
items.display_name: GrepSeek: Training Search Agents for Direct Corpus Interaction
items.summary: Trains a compact search agent to find evidence by issuing shell commands (grep-style) directly against the corpus instead of querying a vector index -- validates the index-free retrieval pattern coding agents already use, and shows how to train for it

items.title: RAPTOR: Recursive Abstractive Processing for Tree-Organized Retrieval
items.tldr: Showed recursively clustering and summarizing chunks into a multi-level tree lets retrieval pull both fine details and high-level themes -- reach for RAPTOR when queries need cross-document synthesis, not simple fact lookup
items.key_contribution: Built a multi-level tree by recursively embedding, clustering, and summarizing text chunks, so retrieval can pull relevant information from both original fine-grained chunks and higher-level generated summaries depending on what a query needs
items.display_name: RAPTOR: Recursive Abstractive Processing for Tree-Organized Retrieval
items.summary: Showed recursively clustering and summarizing chunks into a multi-level tree lets retrieval pull both fine details and high-level themes -- reach for RAPTOR when queries need cross-document synthesis, not simple fact lookup

items.title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
items.tldr: Showed a model can teach itself which API calls to make via self-supervised annotation and perplexity-based filtering, but this approach is now superseded by native function-calling built into current frontier model APIs
items.key_contribution: Showed a language model can self-supervise its own training data for tool use: generating candidate API calls, filtering them by whether they reduce the perplexity of the following text, and fine-tuning on the filtered examples -- with no human-labeled tool-use annotations required
items.display_name: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
items.summary: Showed a model can teach itself which API calls to make via self-supervised annotation and perplexity-based filtering, but this approach is now superseded by native function-calling built into current frontier model APIs

items.title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
items.tldr: PPO: a clipped surrogate objective that keeps policy updates safely small using only first-order optimization — the RL algorithm that, five years later, became the engine of RLHF and thus of ChatGPT-style alignment
items.key_contribution: Replaced trust-region policy optimization's expensive second-order constraint with a simple clipped-ratio objective achieving comparable stability at a fraction of the implementation cost — becoming deep RL's default policy-gradient method and later the standard RLHF optimizer
items.display_name: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
items.summary: PPO: a clipped surrogate objective that keeps policy updates safely small using only first-order optimization — the RL algorithm that, five years later, became the engine of RLHF and thus of ChatGPT-style alignment

items.title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
items.tldr: Introduced GRPO: group-relative policy optimization drops PPO's value network by baselining rewards against groups of sampled outputs — the algorithm behind DeepSeek-R1 and the reasoning-RL wave — plus a 120B-token math corpus mined from Common Crawl
items.key_contribution: Introduced GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization), halving RL training's memory cost by replacing the learned value function with group-normalized reward baselines, and showed careful Common Crawl mining yields a 120B-token math corpus that lifts a 7B model toward much larger models' math performance
items.display_name: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
items.summary: Introduced GRPO: group-relative policy optimization drops PPO's value network by baselining rewards against groups of sampled outputs — the algorithm behind DeepSeek-R1 and the reasoning-RL wave — plus a 120B-token math corpus mined from Common Crawl

items.title: Fast Transformer Decoding: One Write-Head is All You Need (Multi-Query Attention)
items.tldr: Multi-query attention: share one key/value head across all query heads, shrinking the KV cache by the head count and making incremental decoding memory-bandwidth-cheap — the idea GQA later refined and every modern serving stack depends on
items.key_contribution: Identified KV-cache memory bandwidth as the true bottleneck of incremental transformer decoding and fixed it structurally: keys and values get a single shared head while queries keep many, cutting KV-cache size ~h× with minor quality loss
items.display_name: Fast Transformer Decoding: One Write-Head is All You Need (Multi-Query Attention)
items.summary: Multi-query attention: share one key/value head across all query heads, shrinking the KV cache by the head count and making incremental decoding memory-bandwidth-cheap — the idea GQA later refined and every modern serving stack depends on

items.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
items.tldr: Showed agents improve across retries by writing verbal self-reflections on failures into an episodic memory instead of updating weights — 'verbal reinforcement learning' — the retry-with-reflection loop now standard in coding and tool-use agents
items.key_contribution: Reinforced agents through language instead of gradients: after a failed episode, the agent generates a self-reflection diagnosing the failure, stores it in episodic memory, and conditions the next attempt on it — yielding large gains (e.g. 91% HumanEval pass@1 vs GPT-4's 80%) with no fine-tuning
items.display_name: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Showed agents improve across retries by writing verbal self-reflections on failures into an episodic memory instead of updating weights — 'verbal reinforcement learning' — the retry-with-reflection loop now standard in coding and tool-use agents

items.title: RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding
items.tldr: Introduced rotary position embeddings (RoPE), which encode positions by rotating query/key vectors so attention depends on relative distance — now the position encoding of essentially every open LLM and the mechanism behind most context-extension tricks
items.key_contribution: Encoded absolute positions as rotations of query/key pairs whose inner products depend only on relative offsets — a position scheme with no learned parameters, valid at any sequence position, that became the universal default (Llama, Qwen, Gemma, DeepSeek, Mistral all use RoPE)
items.display_name: RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding
items.summary: Introduced rotary position embeddings (RoPE), which encode positions by rotating query/key vectors so attention depends on relative distance — now the position encoding of essentially every open LLM and the mechanism behind most context-extension tricks

items.title: ContextNest: Verifiable Context Governance for Autonomous AI Agent
items.tldr: A governance spec that adds versioned identities, hash chains and point-in-time reconstruction beneath retrieval.
items.key_contribution: Hash-chained version histories make tampering detectable and a specific version addressable, which no metadata-filter approach gives you.
items.display_name: ContextNest: Verifiable Context Governance for Autonomous AI Agent
items.summary: A governance spec that adds versioned identities, hash chains and point-in-time reconstruction beneath retrieval.

items.title: Agent Planning Benchmark: A Diagnostic Framework for Planning Capabilities in LLM Agents
items.tldr: Separates planning from execution with 4,209 multimodal cases covering feedback, tool noise, broken tools, and unsolvable tasks, then tests whether planning diagnostics improve execution.
items.key_contribution: Defines five planning settings across 22 domains and validates plan-focused refinement on ToolSandbox and tau2-bench tasks rather than inferring planning quality from end-to-end success alone.
items.display_name: Agent Planning Benchmark: A Diagnostic Framework for Planning Capabilities in LLM Agents
items.summary: Separates planning from execution with 4,209 multimodal cases covering feedback, tool noise, broken tools, and unsolvable tasks, then tests whether planning diagnostics improve execution.

items.title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks
items.tldr: Framed generation as mapping an input sequence to an output sequence with an encoder-decoder RNN, establishing the seq2seq paradigm that every generative LLM (as prompt-in, text-out) still instantiates
items.key_contribution: Showed a single neural network could read a variable-length input into a fixed vector and decode it into a variable-length output, learning tasks like translation end-to-end without task-specific pipelines
items.display_name: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks
items.summary: Framed generation as mapping an input sequence to an output sequence with an encoder-decoder RNN, establishing the seq2seq paradigm that every generative LLM (as prompt-in, text-out) still instantiates

items.title: A hierarchical memory architecture overcomes context limits in long-horizon multi-agent computational modeling
items.tldr: A multi-agent framework whose capped three-layer memory keeps injected context near 300 tokens over multi-session research work.
items.key_contribution: The context bound is structural rather than aspirational, enforced by category caps and eviction with a reported hard maximum of 4,050 tokens.
items.display_name: A hierarchical memory architecture overcomes context limits in long-horizon multi-agent computational modeling
items.summary: A multi-agent framework whose capped three-layer memory keeps injected context near 300 tokens over multi-session research work.

items.title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
items.tldr: Trained 7B–65B models on public data only, overtraining far past Chinchilla-optimal to optimize inference cost rather than training cost — LLaMA-13B beat GPT-3-175B, and the weights' release ignited the open-model ecosystem
items.key_contribution: Two shifts that defined the open-model era: optimizing for inference-time compute (train smaller models on many more tokens than training-optimal) and demonstrating GPT-3-class quality from exclusively public data — plus the de facto standard architecture recipe (RoPE, SwiGLU, RMSNorm) every open model since has copied
items.display_name: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models

items.title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models

items.key_contribution: Established the Transformer architecture — scaled dot-product self-attention plus multi-head attention and sinusoidal positional encodings — as a complete replacement for recurrent sequence modeling

items.title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
items.tldr: Sample multiple reasoning chains at nonzero temperature and majority-vote the final answers: correct answers are reached by many diverse paths while errors scatter, yielding large accuracy gains at linear compute cost — the founding result of inference-time scaling
items.key_contribution: Replaced greedy CoT decoding with sample-and-marginalize: draw k diverse chains, take the most frequent answer, exploiting the asymmetry that valid reasoning paths converge while flawed ones diverge — +17.9% absolute on GSM8K over greedy CoT and the conceptual basis of test-time compute scaling

items.title: Finetuned Language Models Are Zero-Shot Learners
items.tldr: The FLAN paper: fine-tuning a 137B model on 60+ NLP tasks phrased as natural-language instructions makes it follow instructions on unseen tasks — the founding demonstration of instruction tuning, the step every modern usable LLM undergoes
items.key_contribution: Established instruction tuning as a technique: multi-task fine-tuning on instruction-phrased datasets teaches the general skill of following instructions, improving zero-shot performance on held-out task types — with the crucial caveat that the benefit emerges only at sufficient model scale

items.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
items.tldr: Showed prompting a large enough model to produce intermediate reasoning steps improves multi-step reasoning accuracy -- use CoT for reasoning-heavy tasks, but don't trust the trace as an accurate explanation of the model's actual computation
items.key_contribution: Showed that prompting a sufficiently large language model to produce a chain of intermediate reasoning steps before its final answer substantially improves performance on arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning tasks, and that this benefit only emerges reliably at large model scale

items.title: Jailbroken: How Does LLM Safety Training Fail?
items.tldr: Explained why jailbreaks work via two failure modes — competing objectives (helpfulness vs safety) and mismatched generalization (safety training doesn't cover what pretraining can do) — and showed scale alone won't fix them; the conceptual framework behind LLM red-teaming
items.key_contribution: Provided the first principled taxonomy of jailbreak root causes: safety objectives competing with capability objectives (prefix-injection, refusal-suppression) and safety training failing to generalize across domains pretraining covers (base64, ciphers) — validated by new attacks succeeding on 96%+ of harmful prompts against GPT-4 and Claude v1.3

items.title: MemSyco-Bench: Benchmarking Sycophancy in Agent Memory
items.tldr: Tests whether retrieved memories improve personalization without making an agent treat user-supplied memory as authoritative evidence.
items.key_contribution: Defines five memory-use tests covering factual rejection, scope, evidence conflicts, updates, and valid personalization, then releases a benchmark and resources for agent evaluation.

items.title: SmoothQuant: Accurate and Efficient Post-Training Quantization for Large Language Models
items.tldr: Enables W8A8 (8-bit weight and activation) quantization of LLMs by migrating the quantization difficulty from hard-to-quantize activation outliers into the weights via a per-channel scaling, so both can use simple integer quantization
items.key_contribution: A training-free method that rescales activations and weights by a per-channel factor to 'smooth' activation outliers -- the specific obstacle to low-bit activation quantization in LLMs -- allowing accurate 8-bit weight+activation inference with hardware-friendly integer kernels and near-lossless accuracy

items.title: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks
items.tldr: Discovered 'attention sinks': models dump attention mass on the first few tokens regardless of content, so evicting them collapses windowed attention — keeping just 4 initial tokens plus a sliding window enables stable million-token streaming with no retraining
items.key_contribution: Diagnosed why sliding-window KV eviction fails (softmax must put its probability mass somewhere, and models learn to park it on initial positions) and turned the diagnosis into a zero-training fix: retain the first ~4 tokens' KV alongside the recent window — 22× faster than recomputation with stable perplexity over 4M+ tokens

items.tldr: Benchmarks agents as terminal, software, and social environments change over progressive updates, and evaluates patch-based memory for preserving those changes.

items.tldr: Showed interleaving reasoning traces with external actions and their observations outperforms reasoning-only or acting-only prompting, meaning the reason-act-observe loop should be your default agent architecture pattern before reaching for something more complex
items.key_contribution: Demonstrated that interleaving explicit reasoning traces with actions (like search queries) and their resulting observations, in a single prompted loop, produces more reliable and interpretable task-solving behavior than pure chain-of-thought reasoning or pure action-taking alone
